oneLiner: Turn what's in your fridge into a week of meals you'll actually want to eat.
problem: People waste food and money because they don't know what to cook with the random ingredients they already have, and planning meals from scratch feels like a chore.
targetUser: Busy home cooks (25–45) who want to reduce food waste, save money, and eat better without adding another planning task to their week.
coreFlow: User adds ingredients currently in their fridge (via quick-add tags, categories, or natural language entry).
App suggests a set of recipes that use those ingredients, prioritizing items that need to be used soon.
User selects or tweaks meals for the week and sees a consolidated shopping list for missing items.
User locks in the plan; app provides step-by-step cooking guidance and tracks which ingredients get used.
After the week, user reviews what was cooked vs. wasted, improving future suggestions.

screens.name: My Fridge
screens.purpose: Quickly inventory ingredients on hand, with freshness indicators and easy add/remove.

screens.name: Meal Suggestions
screens.purpose: Browse recipe ideas ranked by how well they match current ingredients and reduce waste.

screens.name: Week Planner
screens.purpose: Drag-and-drop selected meals across the week, see coverage of ingredients, and adjust portions or swap meals.

screens.name: Shopping List
screens.purpose: Aggregated list of only the missing items needed for the chosen meals, organized by aisle.

screens.name: Cook & Track
screens.purpose: Step-by-step recipe view, mark ingredients as used, and log meals cooked vs. wasted.
